survivors.equivalent: `ex.get('command') != 'go'`: a found/answer block whose basis is the current one was reprinted by the line above (reprint raises Out), and one with another basis returns by the second operand, so the first operand never decides

`b.get('basis') != basis(env)` for a go block: a go block is stale only if a command died after it saved a loop or RESTORE_WORK and before render wrote the next BLOCK.json. A stale pending/setup block meets an empty verify (on_verify cleared it before the save; see -7-r); a stale fetch block's files stay in inbox/kit and inbox/pass until invalidate, which also moves BLOCK.json; a local block's inbox/journal files are dropped only by a later commit's post actions, and that commit prints its SAVE blocks (a new BLOCK.json) first. So every file a stale block names is present with its size and the mutant's check finds no code

`ex.get('kind') == 'pending'`: while PENDING.json exists advance runs pending_step first, so every go block of another kind was printed with env.pending None; basis covers PENDING's self_sha256, so with the current basis env.pending is still None and the remaining conjunct is false
`env.pending`: a pending block is printed only while PENDING.json exists and its basis holds PENDING's self_sha256; with PENDING gone the basis differs and go_checks returned above

`env.pending['verify']`: with verify empty, on_verify returns ('ok', None) and changes nothing, and persist rewrites the same document (write_doc's self_sha256 is a function of the content), so the next block is the same

`(env.work or {}).get(ex['loop'])`: a setup block is printed only while RESTORE_WORK holds that loop, and basis covers RESTORE_WORK's self_sha256; with the loop gone the basis differs and go_checks returned above
`env.work[ex['loop']]['verify']`: as GM-cli-go_checks-7-r for a setup loop (save_work rewrites the same RESTORE_WORK)

`phase == 'HEAD'`: the only other session download block is RECHECK's, reached through _commit, which session_next calls only past `if not w.get('head')` (the HEAD download of N), so w['head'] is set and the second conjunct is false there

ENTRY_TOO_LARGE vs PART_TOO_LARGE in block: write_commit refuses an entry or a part over max_upload_bytes before PENDING.json exists, with the same cap (the kit config), so a PENDING loop never reaches this test; a setup loop takes the UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE branch

the same test in on_found: once the entry is confirmed loop['absent'] is [] (see GM-savepoint-block-13-r), so set(loop['absent']) is the empty set either way

`unknown` decides only t['need'] ('verify' or 'done'): while loop['verify'] holds the name's downloads, block prints the DOWNLOAD block without reading need, and on_verify or slip then sets need; with only known ids f['copies'] is set and the name leaves the group, so need is never read
`'verify' if unknown else 'done'`: as GM-savepoint-on_found-4-n, need is not read before on_verify or slip overwrites it

`ex.get('command') != 'go'`: a found/answer block whose basis is the current one was reprinted by the line above (reprint raises Out), and one with another basis returns by the second operand, so the first operand never decides

`b.get('basis') != basis(env)` for a go block: a go block is stale only if a command died after it saved a loop or RESTORE_WORK and before render wrote the next BLOCK.json. A stale pending/setup block meets an empty verify (on_verify cleared it before the save; see -7-r); a stale fetch block's files stay in inbox/kit and inbox/pass until invalidate, which also moves BLOCK.json; a local block's inbox/journal files are dropped only by a later commit's post actions, and that commit prints its SAVE blocks (a new BLOCK.json) first. So every file a stale block names is present with its size and the mutant's check finds no code

`ex.get('kind') == 'pending'`: while PENDING.json exists advance runs pending_step first, so every go block of another kind was printed with env.pending None; basis covers PENDING's self_sha256, so with the current basis env.pending is still None and the remaining conjunct is false
`env.pending`: a pending block is printed only while PENDING.json exists and its basis holds PENDING's self_sha256; with PENDING gone the basis differs and go_checks returned above

`env.pending['verify']`: with verify empty, on_verify returns ('ok', None) and changes nothing, and persist rewrites the same document (write_doc's self_sha256 is a function of the content), so the next block is the same

`(env.work or {}).get(ex['loop'])`: a setup block is printed only while RESTORE_WORK holds that loop, and basis covers RESTORE_WORK's self_sha256; with the loop gone the basis differs and go_checks returned above
`env.work[ex['loop']]['verify']`: as GM-cli-go_checks-7-r for a setup loop (save_work rewrites the same RESTORE_WORK)

`phase == 'HEAD'`: the only other session download block is RECHECK's, reached through _commit, which session_next calls only past `if not w.get('head')` (the HEAD download of N), so w['head'] is set and the second conjunct is false there
`os.path.isdir(target)` in `same`: walk (v1mod.tree_list) lstats the root and raises WALK_UNSUPPORTED_ENTRY ('root') unless it is a directory, which settle catches as same=False
`not os.path.islink(target)` in `same`: tree_list's lstat of a symlink root is not S_ISDIR, so walk raises and settle catches it as same=False
`len(names) == 1`: for two or more names a dict doc is 'count' either way (els=doc is not a list; els=[doc] has length 1)
len([k not in sc]) over the two keys is 2 - len([k in sc]); both differ from 1 exactly when the count is not 1
`s['mode'] == 'everyday'` in dl: R['delivery'] is set only by e55, whose g55 requires not c['Q'], so a qualification run has no prepared_seq
`rid == 'T23' and e['kind'] == 'STAGE'`: _progress returns T23 only through the PROGRESS pair ('T23', 'STAGE', ...), i.e. only for a STAGE
`L['status'] != 'FROZEN'` for B's A chain: g10 requires s['current'] is None (an earlier conjunct) and a Q run that is not FROZEN is the current run (ACTIVE from e_new until e24)

`L['tag'] == 'A-restart1'`: A-restart1 is a restart run (g11 requires restart_of) and g24 refuses restart_eligible true when restart_of is set, so the first operand `not restart_eligible` already holds
g12 `e['kind'] == 'FROZEN'`: the row dispatch calls T12's guard only for kinds {'FROZEN'}

`ro['status'] != 'CONTINUED'` for NO_CONVERSATION: for a CONTINUED role resolution_action returns T48 for every outcome but CONTINUED, whatever forced is (the forced compare and the CONTINUED branch both give T48)

`ro['status'] == 'STARTED'`: both callers pass an open role that is not CONTINUED (forced_for tests status != CONTINUED first and resolution_action requires an OPEN role; session.restore_keys returns for CONTINUED first), and OPEN is {STARTED, CONTINUED}
`oc = q and forced is None and ...`: oc is returned only by T44/T45, reached only after `if forced is not None ...: return 'T47'`, so forced is None there
`oc = ... and item['outcome'] == 'NOTHING_WRITTEN'`: oc is returned only by T44/T45, reached only past `if item['outcome'] != 'NOTHING_WRITTEN' ...: T48`
`not item['ended']` in the T48 line: ended is a bool (checked first) and ended False makes forced_for return NOT_ENDED, which returned T47 above
`item['files_found']` in the T48 line: files_found True makes forced_for return FILES_FOUND, which returned T47 above

`len(need) > 1`: invariant: at most one role is open (a START opens a role only when the run has none open: g20 requires not run_open(R), and only the current run has roles), and the items must equal open(s2)

`ro['status'] == 'STARTED'`: both callers pass an open role that is not CONTINUED (forced_for tests status != CONTINUED first and resolution_action requires an OPEN role; session.restore_keys returns for CONTINUED first), and OPEN is {STARTED, CONTINUED}
`oc = q and forced is None and ...`: oc is returned only by T44/T45, reached only after `if forced is not None ...: return 'T47'`, so forced is None there
`oc = ... and item['outcome'] == 'NOTHING_WRITTEN'`: oc is returned only by T44/T45, reached only past `if item['outcome'] != 'NOTHING_WRITTEN' ...: T48`
`not item['ended']` in the T48 line: ended is a bool (checked first) and ended False makes forced_for return NOT_ENDED, which returned T47 above
`item['files_found']` in the T48 line: files_found True makes forced_for return FILES_FOUND, which returned T47 above

`len(need) > 1`: invariant: at most one role is open (a START opens a role only when the run has none open: g20 requires not run_open(R), and only the current run has roles), and the items must equal open(s2)
`not c['Q']` before the INPUTS test: status INPUTS is set only by e15, whose g15 requires not c['Q'], so a qualification run is never INPUTS

loop['phase'] is an informational field of PENDING.json (spec §5.1 step 3) that no code reads (savepoint, cli and maint never read it back)

ENTRY_TOO_LARGE vs PART_TOO_LARGE in block: write_commit refuses an entry or a part over max_upload_bytes before PENDING.json exists, with the same cap (the kit config), so a PENDING loop never reaches this test; a setup loop takes the UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE branch

`loop['entry']['copies'] is None` for the absent names: on_found empties loop['absent'] in the first call of the loop (the entry is the first group, still unconfirmed then; t_d11_on_found_handback_and_absent), and the entry is confirmed only in that call or in on_verify after it, so a confirmed entry always has absent == []
the same test in on_found: once the entry is confirmed loop['absent'] is [] (see GM-savepoint-block-13-r), so set(loop['absent']) is the empty set either way

`unknown` decides only t['need'] ('verify' or 'done'): while loop['verify'] holds the name's downloads, block prints the DOWNLOAD block without reading need, and on_verify or slip then sets need; with only known ids f['copies'] is set and the name leaves the group, so need is never read
`'verify' if unknown else 'done'`: as GM-savepoint-on_found-4-n, need is not read before on_verify or slip overwrites it

`ex.get('command') != 'go'`: a found/answer block whose basis is the current one was reprinted by the line above (reprint raises Out), and one with another basis returns by the second operand, so the first operand never decides

`b.get('basis') != basis(env)` for a go block: a go block is stale only if a command died after it saved a loop or RESTORE_WORK and before render wrote the next BLOCK.json. A stale pending/setup block meets an empty verify (on_verify cleared it before the save; see -7-r); a stale fetch block's files stay in inbox/kit and inbox/pass until invalidate, which also moves BLOCK.json; a local block's inbox/journal files are dropped only by a later commit's post actions, and that commit prints its SAVE blocks (a new BLOCK.json) first. So every file a stale block names is present with its size and the mutant's check finds no code

`ex.get('kind') == 'pending'`: while PENDING.json exists advance runs pending_step first, so every go block of another kind was printed with env.pending None; basis covers PENDING's self_sha256, so with the current basis env.pending is still None and the remaining conjunct is false
`env.pending`: a pending block is printed only while PENDING.json exists and its basis holds PENDING's self_sha256; with PENDING gone the basis differs and go_checks returned above

`env.pending['verify']`: with verify empty, on_verify returns ('ok', None) and changes nothing, and persist rewrites the same document (write_doc's self_sha256 is a function of the content), so the next block is the same

`(env.work or {}).get(ex['loop'])`: a setup block is printed only while RESTORE_WORK holds that loop, and basis covers RESTORE_WORK's self_sha256; with the loop gone the basis differs and go_checks returned above
`env.work[ex['loop']]['verify']`: as GM-cli-go_checks-7-r for a setup loop (save_work rewrites the same RESTORE_WORK)

`phase == 'HEAD'`: the only other session download block is RECHECK's, reached through _commit, which session_next calls only past `if not w.get('head')` (the HEAD download of N), so w['head'] is set and the second conjunct is false there
`os.path.isdir(target)` in `same`: walk (v1mod.tree_list) lstats the root and raises WALK_UNSUPPORTED_ENTRY ('root') unless it is a directory, which settle catches as same=False
`not os.path.islink(target)` in `same`: tree_list's lstat of a symlink root is not S_ISDIR, so walk raises and settle catches it as same=False
`len(names) == 1`: for two or more names a dict doc is 'count' either way (els=doc is not a list; els=[doc] has length 1)
len([k not in sc]) over the two keys is 2 - len([k in sc]); both differ from 1 exactly when the count is not 1
